samples.text:
The line graph shows the number of electric vehicles in one country from 2016 to 2024, and the bar chart shows the number of public charging points in four regions in 2016 and 2024.

Overall, the number of electric vehicles increased very fast, and the charging points also increased in all region, specially in the capital.

In 2016 there was only 45 thousand electric vehicles. In 2018 the number increased to 110 thousand and in 2020 it was 260 thousand. After that, the growth was faster and it reached 620 thousand in 2022. In 2024 the number was 1,150 thousand, which is more than 25 times higher than 2016.

The bar chart shows that the capital had the most charging points in both years. It had 1.8 thousand in 2016 and it increased to 19.5 thousand in 2024. The other regions had much less. The North increased from 0.4 thousand to 4.1 thousand, the Central from 0.6 thousand to 7.8 thousand and the South from 0.5 thousand to 6.2 thousand. So the North had the smallest number of charging points in both years.
samples.why: Basic overview present · all figures accurate but reported one after another · simple, repetitive linking and verbs · some awkward word choice (specially) · errors in agreement, quantifiers and articles.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates the growth in the number of electric vehicles in use in one country between 2016 and 2024, and the bar chart compares the number of public charging points in four regions at the start and end of this period.

Overall, the number of electric vehicles increased exponentially, and there was a substantial rise in charging points in every region, with the capital having by far the most in both years.

In 2016, there were just 45 thousand electric vehicles. This figure more than doubled to 110 thousand by 2018 and to 260 thousand by 2020. Growth then accelerated even further, with the number reaching 620 thousand in 2022 and 1,150 thousand in 2024, which is over 25 times the 2016 level.

Regarding charging points, the capital had 1.8 thousand in 2016, more than the other three regions combined, and this number rose more than tenfold to 19.5 thousand in 2024. The Central region saw the most rapid growth, from 0.6 thousand to 7.8 thousand, a thirteen-fold increase. The South and the North also experienced significant increases, from 0.5 thousand to 6.2 thousand and from 0.4 thousand to 4.1 thousand respectively, but North remained the region with the fewest points.
samples.why: Clear overview of both visuals · key features highlighted with useful multiples · logical organisation and good cohesion · some less common vocabulary (exponentially, tenfold) · one minor article slip.

samples.text:
The line graph shows how many electric vehicles were in use in one country from 2016 to 2024, while the bar chart compares the provision of public charging points across four regions in 2016 and 2024.

Electric vehicle numbers grew at an accelerating rate throughout the period, and charging infrastructure expanded dramatically in all four regions, although the capital retained a commanding lead.

From a modest base of 45 thousand in 2016, the number of electric vehicles more than doubled in each two-year interval up to 2022, when it reached 620 thousand. It then climbed by a further 530 thousand to 1,150 thousand in 2024, roughly 25 times the initial figure.

The number of charging points increased at least tenfold in every region. The capital, which already had 1.8 thousand points in 2016, had 19.5 thousand by 2024, more than the other three regions combined (18.1 thousand). Proportionally, however, the fastest expansion took place in the Central region, where provision rose thirteenfold from 0.6 to 7.8 thousand. The South also grew rapidly, from 0.5 to 6.2 thousand, while the North, starting from the lowest base of 0.4 thousand, still had the fewest points in 2024, at 4.1 thousand.
samples.why: Skilful overview · data selected and compared precisely (multiples, combined totals) · sophisticated cohesion between absolute and proportional change · precise vocabulary (provision, infrastructure, commanding lead) · wide range of error-free structures.
